> Not sure what is going on though!

I'm not entirely sure either, to be honest. Do you have a way to reproduce it?

Thoughts on trying the following and seeing if it reoccurs? 
https://github.com/rclone/rclone/compare/master...nielash:rclone:8815-bisync-race-in-concurrent-tests

https://github.com/nielash/rclone/actions/runs/17657262494
Thanks, this looks very helpful! Haven't had a chance yet to take a close look (busy week for me) but I plan to.

My analysis of the `CaptureOutput` race was wrong - what is happening is that there are still users of the logging function after `fun()` has returned. This was easily fixed with a mutex. This probably shouldn't happen though - it perhaps indicates there is some synchronisation missing between ending the bisync and running go routines. I got gemini to write a script to run bisync 100 times using the command line you gave above to have something more reproducable to test
The script

```sh #!/bin/bash # --- Configuration --- # The total number of times to run the test loop. TOTAL_RUNS=100 # The specific Go test command to execute. TEST_COMMAND="go test -count=1 -run '^TestBisyncConcurrent$' ./cmd/bisync -race -v" # A directory to store logs from failed runs. LOG_DIR="test_failures" # --- Script Start --- echo "Starting test runner..." # Initialize a counter for failed test runs. failures=0 # Create the log directory if it doesn't exist. mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR" # Loop from 1 to TOTAL_RUNS. for i in $(seq 1 $TOTAL_RUNS) do echo "--- Running iteration $i of $TOTAL_RUNS ---" # Define a unique log file name for this iteration. LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/failure_run_${i}.log" # Execute the Go test command. # The `&>` operator redirects both standard output and standard error to the log file. eval $TEST_COMMAND &> "$LOG_FILE" # Check the exit code of the last command (`eval`). # A non-zero exit code indicates a test failure. if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then # Increment the failure counter. failures=$((failures + 1)) echo "🔴 FAILED: Iteration $i failed. Log saved to: $LOG_FILE" else # If the test was successful, print a success message and remove the log file. echo "✅ PASSED: Iteration $i passed." rm "$LOG_FILE" fi done # --- Final Report --- echo "-------------------------------------" echo "Test run complete." ```

I then hunted and killed the races! Before any fixes 88/100 failures With - `accounting: make MaxCompletedTransfers atomic to fix bisync race` c56fffc48a6b5697bcc3fc75822458b5f008c3bd 3/100 failures - 2 of which are the CaptureOutput race With - `accounting: make MaxCompletedTransfers atomic to fix bisync race` c56fffc48a6b5697bcc3fc75822458b5f008c3bd - `bisync: fix race when CaptureOutput is used concurrently` 4f619b45bca8f98a36de00cf16fcec61e361364d 1/100 failures - no races! The last failure is here - it seems to be to do with partial files. Perhaps something to do with the IDs clashing? Not sure - haven't investigated. [failure_run_6.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22451767/failure_run_6.log) Here is the branch so far [fix-8815-bisync-race](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-8815-bisync-race)

Very clever!

Both of those fixes look good to me.

> The last failure is here - it seems to be to do with partial files. Perhaps something to do with the IDs clashing? Not sure - haven't investigated.

After a lot of trial and error, I found that I was able to reliably reproduce this by adding `-pcount 20` (20 parallel tests instead of 2), and then I was able to reliably fix it by using `t.TempDir()` instead of `os.TempDir()`. https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/fa3030d52f07a20fc48086d537a5ae551038dff0

Also I think your atomic fix is missing this: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commit/e5dcce8d1d566b15cb6fd44dbaa4b8d96bcc195f

My branch based on yours: https://github.com/nielash/rclone/commits/fix-8815-bisync-race-2/

Should we add your script to `./bin`? Seems like a useful test pattern for all sorts of stuff.

Well done with the final fix :-) And thanks for fixing my fix also!

> accounting: make MaxCompletedTransfers atomic to fix bisync race c56fffc

This fix is a bandaid though. The problem is that `MaxCompletedTransfers` is a global variable and two runs of bisync can still interfere with each other (in a non racy fashion now!).

Perhaps we should make it a Config variable instead for `MaxCompletedTransfers` - then we can set it in `ctx`? Would that work for you?

You're right, that would be a lot better. I wonder if maybe it should be a `(s *StatsInfo)` method, and different stats groups could have different settings.

I also wonder if maybe bisync should have a flag to opt out of forcing it to `-1`, for users who don't plan to use the graceful shutdown feature and would rather have the memory savings...

> Should we add your script to ./bin? Seems like a useful test pattern for all sorts of stuff.

```
cd cmd/bisync

```

I've been looking at the use of MaxCompletedTransfers in bisync

This makes sense

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/5d6d79e7d4392924d1e642ece804ff5d7e8c3f91/cmd/bisync/queue.go#L248-L251

But I'm struggling to understand this - `PruneTransfers()` clears at most one done transfer but bisync is expecting it to clear all the done transfers I think.

https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/5d6d79e7d4392924d1e642ece804ff5d7e8c3f91/cmd/bisync/listing.go#L709-L711

I think this should be calling something which prunes all the done transfers.

I'll add that and a global config to configure the MaxCompletedTransfers in a moment.

I think this is all fixed now!

Would you mind giving this the once-over @nielash ?

Foo - that had a bisync failure: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/actions/runs/17972959950/job/51119728765 not one on the concurrent tests though. Any ideas?

I think I see the issue. Changing `os.TempDir()` to `t.TempDir()` has made the filenames too long (the session name is derived from the full path).

There is an existing issue about this [here](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/5678#issuecomment-1997594839), which I was planning to address as part of the sessions project on that ticket, but that's a much larger project. Perhaps it makes more sense to address it now with a smaller fix. Essentially, adding a new flag to customize the session name and/or use md5 hashes instead of very long paths.
